transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As we prepare for this afternoon's medication safety review of the new intravenous anticoagulant protocol, I'd like to hear from each of you on any operational findings before I make my final decision on safeguards. Let's start with pharmacy — any issues you've identified with stocking, labeling, or preparation of the medication in the automated dispensing cabinets?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I've verified three selection errors involving the 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL anticoagulant concentrations since Monday. Pharmacy can remove bedside stock and supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during a temporary hold.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: From the laboratory medicine side, I need to flag a monitoring issue. Our anti-Xa analyzer is unavailable for calibration until Friday at 17:00. During that period, the lab's approved replacement for monitoring patients on this protocol is an aPTT test every six hours. We need to make sure nursing and clinical IT are aware that aPTT, not anti-Xa, will be used for monitoring until Friday evening.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: From nursing education, I need to flag a staffing competency issue. My competency roster shows that 18 nurses scheduled for tonight's shift have not yet completed the new anticoagulant administration module. Under our current policy, each of those nurses must receive charge-nurse sign-off before they can administer this medication. Morgan, this is something we'll need to account for in any safeguards you decide on for the night shift.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: From clinical information technology, I can confirm that a high-priority electronic medication-record alert can be deployed at 16:00 today. This alert will warn clinicians about concentration selection and require acknowledgment before the order can be released. This aligns with the timing of our afternoon safety review and could serve as an additional safeguard for the night shift.
transcript.speaker: A5

decisions.safety_protocol: Temporary hold on bedside stock of the IV anticoagulant; pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes only, effective for tonight's night shift pending full safety review completion.
decisions.dispensing_concentration: Standardize to pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes only; remove both 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL concentrations from automated dispensing cabinets at bedside to eliminate selection errors.
decisions.laboratory_monitoring: Use aPTT every six hours as the approved monitoring test for patients on this protocol until the anti-Xa analyzer is calibrated and available on Friday at 17:00. Nursing and clinical IT must be notified of this substitution.
decisions.nurse_authorization: All 18 nurses who have not completed the anticoagulant administration module must receive charge-nurse sign-off before administering this medication on tonight's shift.
decisions.electronic_alert: Deploy the high-priority electronic medication-record alert at 16:00 today, warning clinicians about concentration selection and requiring acknowledgment before the order can be released.

commitments.detail: Remove bedside stock of both concentrations from automated dispensing cabinets and supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during the temporary hold.
Communicate to nursing and clinical IT that aPTT every six hours is the approved monitoring substitute until anti-Xa analyzer calibration on Friday at 17:00.
Ensure charge-nurse sign-off is enforced for all 18 non-competency-completed nurses on tonight's shift before they administer this anticoagulant.
Deploy the high-priority concentration-selection alert in the electronic medication record at 16:00 today with mandatory acknowledgment before order release.
Reassess all temporary safeguards after Friday at 17:00 when anti-Xa analyzer calibration is complete and full protocol monitoring can resume.
